family_title_en: Read two-syllable words: open and closed syllables

stages.ix_title: Read two-syllable words: open and closed syllables

prompt.en: Is the first syllable open or closed?
prompt.ko: 첫 음절은 열린 음절인가요, 닫힌 음절인가요?

what_to_do.ko: 열린 음절 또는 닫힌 음절을 누르세요.

roots: Keep the choice order open then closed on every item. Never add a choice.
The stem is exactly one two-syllable word. Judge its first syllable only.
The wrong tap is the other type. No word may be both open and closed.
Open means the first syllable ends in a vowel and that vowel says its name.
Closed means the first syllable ends in a consonant and that vowel is short.
Skip a first syllable that is schwa, r-controlled, or a vowel team.
Skip silent-e and consonant-le words, and skip words that are not two syllables.
Tier 3 is a VCV near miss that looks easy to split the wrong way.
Use kid words about school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather. No brands.
Do not use a real name, and do not use the stem open or the stem closed.

tier_rules.1: One easy two-syllable word. Closed words show a doubled consonant, like rabbit. Open words show a clear long vowel, like baby.
tier_rules.2: A grade-level two-syllable word with a reliable first vowel. The split is clear, but no doubled consonant gives it away.
tier_rules.3: A VCV near miss. Closed words such as study look open. Open words such as student or label look closed. The vowel sound decides.

open_syl.en: An open syllable ends in a vowel. That vowel says its name.
open_syl.ko: 열린 음절은 모음으로 끝납니다. 그 모음은 자기 이름을 말합니다.

closed_syl.en: A closed syllable ends in a consonant. That vowel stays short.
closed_syl.ko: 닫힌 음절은 자음으로 끝납니다. 그 모음은 짧은 소리입니다.

open_vcv.en: Split after the first vowel. It says its name, so the syllable is open.
open_vcv.ko: 첫 모음 뒤에서 나누세요. 모음이 자기 이름을 말하므로 열린 음절입니다.

closed_vcv.en: The first vowel is short. End that syllable with a consonant. It is closed.
closed_vcv.ko: 첫 모음은 짧은 소리입니다. 그 음절을 자음으로 끝내면 닫힌 음절입니다.
